question: Should OpenClaw accept an opt-in deny-over-allow exec policy persisted in both openclaw.json and exec-approvals.json and exposed through the gateway protocol?
rationale: Source and live proof establish that the implementation works, but they cannot choose the permanent security contract, parallel policy ownership, or operator-facing configuration surface.

options.title: Accept the dual-layer contract
options.body: Keep both persisted surfaces unioned, with human-only one-shot approval on matches and fail-closed handling for unanalyzable commands.

options.title: Narrow to approvals policy
options.body: Retain the STOP list only in exec-approvals.json and its protocol, removing the parallel openclaw.json option.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Keep the canonical issue open but do not land a denylist until the exec policy model is redesigned.

recommendation.title: Accept the dual-layer contract
recommendation.body: Keep both persisted surfaces unioned, with human-only one-shot approval on matches and fail-closed handling for unanalyzable commands.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal across the central exec policy and host security paths makes this the best available decision owner.
